title: Repeated likes produce one like and one notification with no side effects

cases.note: Same test — exactly one intro_like_notifications row, deduped by (recipient, intro, actor).

intro_likes.rs::a_like_creates_no_relationship — the only rows a like produces are the like and its notification; intro_like_notifications has no state/pending/accepted/approval/deadline column (asserted through information_schema).
intro_likes.rs::withdrawing_a_heart_removes_the_notification (still visible: like_count 0) and delete_by_a_viewer_who_lost_access_returns_a_null_count (not visible: like_count null).
intro_likes.rs::an_author_cannot_like_their_own_post — LikeError::SelfLike from the command, and constraint intro_likes_no_self_like from the database.
intro_likes.rs::a_non_author_liker_list_is_403 — 403 for the liker and for a stranger, 200 for the author.
ActivityFeed.test.tsx — a like entry opens the liker's profile and no entry carries an approval affordance.

limitations: The notification is written to intro_like_notifications (migration 0087), not to the notification-service's own table. Wiring that projection into the notification service is a separate composition step; the dedupe and the one-row guarantee are proven here.
